name: Carioca
description: Carioca is an Argentinean Contract Rummy variant similar to Central American Loba. Played over 7 rounds with increasingly difficult contracts. Players try to meld trios (three of a kind) and escaleras (4-card straight flushes) to get rid of all cards. Features wild jokers and the ability to add to other players' melds.

content.text: Carioca is an Argentinean Contract Rummy variant similar to Central American Loba. Played over 7 rounds with increasingly difficult contracts. Players try to meld trios (three of a kind) and escaleras (4-card straight flushes) to get rid of all cards. Features wild jokers and the ability to add to other players' melds.

Carioca is an Argentinean variant of Contract Rummy, closely related to Central American Loba. The game was documented by Eduardo Valcarcel as played in Argentina. It differs from Loba primarily in having 7 rounds instead of 6.
2-5 players, each playing individually (no partnerships). Deal and play are counter-clockwise.
Two standard 52-card packs plus 4 jokers = 108 cards total. Jokers are wild. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 (Ace high or low in escaleras).
First dealer chosen at random. Deal passes to the right (counter-clockwise). Rounds 1-6: 11 cards each. Round 7: 12 cards each. One card turned up to start discard pile; remainder forms draw pile.
